differences.text: The skip link has `href="#"` and moves focus to the main region itself: a fragment target inside a shadow root cannot be resolved by fragment navigation or by the axe `skip-link` rule.

The mobile breakpoint comes from the registered theme (`widthBreakpoints`) when it declares one, else from the default set (sm 640, md 768, lg 1024, xl 1280, 2xl 1536); `mobile-nav-breakpoint` picks the key (default md). The media query is `(width < Npx)`, so the edge belongs to the wider layout. There are no breakpoint tokens.
A consumer `tct-mobile-nav` in the `mobile-nav` slot replaces the automatic drawer and the toggle stays enabled; upstream disables the toggle then.

Additive API: `no-mobile-nav`, `no-mobile-toggle`, `mobile-nav-open`, `default-is-mobile` (first paint and server rendering), `no-landmarks` (a shell inside a page that already has banner and main landmarks, for previews and embedded apps), the `--app-shell-height` custom property (a shell in a bounded frame), the `drawer` and `mobile-bar` slots, and the methods `openMobileNav`, `closeMobileNav` and `focusMain`. `tct-open-change` reports the drawer.
The variants paint --color-background-body (wash) and --color-background-surface; the elevated variant draws a rounded start corner with --radius-page behind a transparent main region.

requests.reason: WP-14 (top nav, side nav) consumes appShellMobileContext (app-shell/app-shell-mobile.context.ts) through AppShellMobileController, and provides the `drawer` and `mobile-bar` slot content when it needs to replace the automatic ones.
